hypothesis: A nominal sample interval in a frozen manifest can contradict the hashed CSV's observed gaps even when the existing <=60 s CSV gap check passes.
baseline: capture_alignment.py v1 (source blob 91aeb332397e067fa8f53de66ef9db2bbf967db5) did not compare observed gaps to manifest sample_interval_s
method: Reject any observed consecutive CSV timestamp gap outside 0.5x to 1.5x the declared nominal interval, with 1e-6 s arithmetic slack; provisional review gate, not calibrated timing tolerance.
dataset: Temporary synthetic 60 W cooling CSV bundles; no hardware or real measurements

execution.command: python -B -m unittest -v test_fixture_origin_gate.py test_dry_run_integrity.py test_capture_chain.py test_capture_alignment.py

limitations: Hash consistency does not authenticate physical origin or prove logger-to-CSV conversion.
Fixed nominal cadence assumption may reject valid event-driven or variable-rate logger recordings.
50% cadence tolerance is provisional, not calibrated or derived from a timing standard.
Fictional consistent data can pass; no real cooling, comfort, safety or efficiency measured.
decision: Keep draft/unmerged; add cadence review gate without advancing maturity; require real physical logger dry run and controlled comparisons.
next_experiment: Issue #15: inventory actual instruments and uncertainties, freeze nominal cadence, capture original >=10 minute logger bytes, replay conversion, inspect gaps/energy/geometry and preserve negative findings.
